$comment: The release set (P7-D): the catalog entries a new Sigil install fetches without the user choosing anything (defaults), and the light options the app offers next to them. scripts/release/check-catalog-pins.mjs holds every member to a stricter rule than build.rs applies to the rest of the catalog: published, hash-pinned, every source immutable, every digest independent of the download (no trust-on-first-use), and the same for everything the member requires.

Heavy and GPU-only models (Cohere, Qwen3-ASR 1.7B, Voxtral, the 7B+ translators, Qwen3-TTS, Magpie, Breeze, OmniVoice, Fish S2, Chatterbox) are opt-in and unbenchmarked in P7. They are still published, so build.rs and the global check require them to be hash-pinned, but they are not in this set.

Selectors: 'ids' are exact catalog ids (each must exist); 'prefixes' match every catalog id that starts with the text (each must match at least one). The CPU speech models and runtimes of src-tauri/model-catalog/stt-routing.json must all be in 'defaults' (the check reads the routing table), so changing the routing table without this file fails the check.
Edit this file when a default or a light option changes, then run: node scripts/release/check-catalog-pins.mjs

stt-cpu.why: Local speech-to-text on the processor: Nemotron streaming partials, Parakeet Ultra finals (Parakeet v3 behind it), SenseVoice (ja, zh), Qwen3-ASR 0.6B (ko and the languages nothing else covers), spoken-language ID for auto mode, Whisper for everything else. Rows of stt-routing.json after the P7-A campaign.

translation.why: The bundled translator chain: Hy-MT2 1.8B on llama-server (Vulkan, or the CPU build), then NLLB-200 600M. Firefox Translations (Bergamot) sits between them when its pack is imported (see allowUnpublished).

tts.why: The local voice a new desktop install offers: Kokoro v1.0 through Sigil's own ONNX Runtime session (Windows SAPI needs nothing).

voice-changer.why: What the RVC voice changer needs apart from the content encoder: the MIT default voice and the pitch models its presets use (the encoder is a Sigil export and stays import-only).

stt-light.why: Cheaper speech options: the 160 ms Nemotron, Moonshine (English), every Whisper size up to small (and their quantizations), the Vosk small models, Smart Turn (commit hints) and the music gate.

translation-light.why: The 1.25-bit Hy-MT2 for PCs that cannot spare 1.1 GB, and the 106 Firefox Translations (Bergamot) directions (36-70 MB each, no graphics memory), which run on the Sigil-built helper pack that is imported, not downloaded.

tts-light.why: Small local voices: Kitten, Piper (36 voices), Pocket TTS, the Mandarin Kokoro and the shared Japanese dictionary Kokoro and the readings use.

voice-changer-light.why: Noise suppression for the voice changer's conditioned copy.

vr.why: The SteamVR overlay's OpenVR runtime (loaded lazily, never launches SteamVR).

gpu-packs.why: The opt-in GPU runtimes: NVIDIA's CUDA 13 / cuDNN 9 libraries and the CUDA llama-server. Large (1.9 GB and 0.6 GB), so never part of the defaults.

allowUnpublished.why: Firefox Translations needs a Sigil-built helper (ADR 0008) that is built by scripts/runtime-packs/bergamot/build.ps1 and imported; asset hosting is local only. Without the pack the translator chain skips it and falls through to NLLB.

tofu.why: alphacephei.com publishes only md5 digests, so the sha256 of each Vosk model was taken from one download (pin-catalog --hash-by-download). Legacy engine. vosk/small-en-us-0.15 matches a copy the app downloaded in April 2026, long before the pin; the other ten come from one download each (re-hash them with --hash-by-download --max-download-mb 90 when convenient).

attested.by: The sha256 of each Firefox Translations model is the one Mozilla's model registry (Remote Settings, translations-models) publishes with the attachment. Re-check with: node scripts/runtime-packs/bergamot/gen-catalog.mjs --check. The check here cannot read it.

rollingTags.why: k2-fsa keeps adding assets to this release. Pinned by sha256, so a replaced asset fails the hash check instead of installing; a removed asset needs a mirror (a 'github-release' source on Mewnah/Sigil assets-v1, uploaded by the user).
Same rolling release (Pocket TTS, sherpa-packaged Piper/Kitten/Kokoro archives).
